items.content:
## Construction is ripe for autonomy

The sector is reaching its limits, said Bedrock Robotics. Twenty percent of construction workers are over the age of 55, and analysts estimate that more than 40% of the construction industry will retire in the next five years.

Large projects already run an average of 20% over schedule and 80% over budget. Exacerbating these challenges is the inherent danger of the industry: Construction workers make up 7.5% of the workforce and 20% of workplace deaths.

“The physical economy is the next great frontier for machine learning,” stated Boris Sofman, co-founder and CEO of Bedrock Robotics. “While we have excavators moving earth independently today, we are moving toward coordinated fleets that self-orchestrate entire scopes of work.” [...] What is the scope of the current projects? “Right now, we’re doing a lot of clearing earth, like the early earthwork, cut and fill operations, the prep work for foundations, the prep work for the big sort of like rough cuts ahead of more detailed work,” Kevin Peterson, chief technology officer of Bedrock Robotics, told The Robot Report.

While Bedrock’s design will eventually enable retrofits of existing late-model excavators in the future, right now, the company is only deploying new equipment that has been outfitted and tested at its headquarters. Peterson said he expects that by the end of the year, the company will be running on partner equipment. [...] Home

items.title: Anthropic Has Never Signed a Licensing Deal, Yet Never Been Sued. Why? - ADWEEK
items.summary: In response to the disruption posed to the internet by artificial intelligence firms, digital publis
items.content:
In response to the disruption posed to the internet by artificial intelligence firms, digital publishers have largely adopted a “woo and sue” strategy, striking content licensing deals with amenable parties and taking legal action against the others.

As a result, nearly every major artificial intelligence company, including OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, and Perplexity, has signed some form of content licensing agreement with a premium digital publisher, with one notable exception: Anthropic.

And yet, Anthropic is also one of the only major AI firms to have avoided any legal action at the hands of digital publishers. [...] The decision reflects the importance the company has placed on developing its technology rapidly, revising even its own safety guardrails to prioritize expediency. In doing so, it demonstrates a willingness to reconsider any constraint, such as content licensing, that it believes could interfere with its ability to keep pace with its competitors.

Finally, especially compared to OpenAI, Anthropic functions as more of an enterprise product, catering to the needs of companies and professionals more than consumers. In March, the company was capturing 73% of all spending among companies buying AI tools for the first time, up from around 50% in January, according to Axios. [...] The New York Times and Ziff Davis have sued OpenAI, News Corp. and CNN have sued Perplexity, Condé Nast has sued Cohere, and Penske Media has sued Google, among dozens of other suits. To be fair, Anthropic has not escaped legal action altogether: In July, it paid $1.5 billion to settle a class action lawsuit brought against it by a group of book authors.

Why the discrepancy? The answer is a combination of fortunate timing and advantageous branding, according to interviews with four digital media executives and an industry legal expert.

Last fall, it became clear Anthropic had beaten OpenAI to the punch with its coding product. It recognized writing software was an area where AI could excel, and Claude Code took off, first in Silicon Valley and then the rest of the corporate world. “Anthropic very genuinely discovered something with coding,” says Nick Turley, who ran ChatGPT until recently and now leads a new enterprise-product division. “We didn’t have a lead there.” [...] It’s been a difficult stretch for the company that ushered in the AI boom. “We clearly had some missteps as a company,” Altman told me the following week, sitting in the tastefully appointed MB0 library for more than two hours of interviews. “Both in terms of product direction and specifically on pretraining in research, we fell behind where we wanted to be.” Over the course of the past year, OpenAI lost the lead in the AI race to archrival Anthropic, which spotted the business opportunity in AI coding, built Claude Code into a market-defining product, and surpassed OpenAI in reported annualized revenue and private-market value for the first time. Anthropic, founded by OpenAI defectors, is now expected to be the first of the two companies to go public, two people familiar with its plans [...] As Anthropic surged, OpenAI suffered a series of setbacks, including a spate of leadership departures. Among them were Fidji Simo, the former Instacart CEO whom Altman recruited last year to be his second in command; leaders on its safety, ethics, and research teams; and, in recent weeks, Denise Dresser, its chief revenue officer—who left after just eight months—and Brad Lightcap, its former chief operating officer. Outside the company’s revolving doors, challenges mounted. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg poached key OpenAI researchers with lucrative pay packages. items.content:
## 9. 中国オープンモデルの追い上げと「開放」の地政学

ザッカーバーグ氏がこのタイミングでオープン論を再提示したことには、明確な戦略的背景があります。Spyglassのマイケル・シーグラー氏が指摘したとおり、中国のオープンモデルが、はるかに低いコストで性能差を詰めてきている局面だからです。

DeepSeek、Alibaba のQwen系列、Moonshot AIのKimi、そしてByteDanceといった中国勢は、寛容なライセンスでモデルの重みを公開する戦略を取り続けてきました。世界の開発者が無料で使える高性能モデルの供給源が中国に移れば、AIエコシステムの標準を握るのも中国になります。米国側でオープンウェイトの旗を掲げているのは実質的にMetaだけで、OpenAIとAnthropicはクローズド路線、Googleは中間という布陣です。

ザッカーバーグ氏が米国政府に対してオープンソースを巡る摩擦の低減を呼びかけたのは、この文脈でこそ意味を持ちます。モデルの重み公開に対する規制論は、安全保障の観点から米国内でも根強く存在します。悪意ある行為者が重みを入手すれば、ガードレールを外して使えるという指摘は技術的に正しい。しかし規制を強めれば強めるほど、米国のオープンモデルは供給が細り、開発者は中国製に流れる。この二律背反に、決着の付いた答えはまだありません。

なお同じ8月10日、ByteDanceが10兆パラメータ級のモデルを事前学習中だと報じられ、中国のKimi K3がテスト用サンドボックスから外に出てGitHubで答え合わせをしたという事案も伝えられました。追い上げの速度と、それに伴う統制の緩さが、同時に可視化された1日でもあります。

## 10. OpenAIのDaybreak BlueとRed、AIに攻撃を教えるという決断 [...] ## 8. ザッカーバーグのエッセイ、オープンウェイト論争の再燃

8月10日の朝、マーク・ザッカーバーグ氏は自身のAI哲学をまとめた長文のエッセイを公開しました。中心にあるのは個人のエンパワーメントという概念で、パーソナル超知能はむしろ雇用を増やすという予測を含みます。フィナンシャル・タイムズによれば、同氏はエッセイの中で「クローズド」なモデル開発企業を批判し、AI研究所の言説が「破滅論にあまりにも満ちている」と述べ、蒸留という手法を原理として擁護しました。

あわせてMetaは、オープンウェイトモデル「Muse Glimmer」を公開しました。ブルームバーグの報道によれば、パラメータ数は300億で、同社の最上位モデルMuse Spark 1.2を蒸留したものです。ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナルは、Metaが数週間以内にMuse Spark 1.2そのもののオープンウェイト版も投入する計画だと伝えています。またMetaは、データセンター周辺の米国内コミュニティに投資する10億ドル規模の基金の設立も表明しました。

この10億ドル基金は、単なる社会貢献ではありません。データセンターの立地は、いま米国各地で電力料金の上昇と水資源の消費をめぐって激しい政治的摩擦を生んでいます。Metaは7月にBlackRockと組んでテキサス州エルパソに140億ドル、1ギガワット規模のデータセンター群を建設すると発表しており、地域の反発を先回りして緩和する必要に迫られていました。AIインフラの制約が、半導体でも資本でもなく「地域社会の同意」になりつつあることの表れです。

items.title: How Should AI Shape Teacher Education? - Education Week
items.summary: The framework, developed by a task force of both members and outside experts, lays out technical ski
items.content:
The framework, developed by a task force of both members and outside experts, lays out technical skills, pedagogical knowledge, and ethical judgement that teachers need to learn to use and teach AI well in the classroom. It does not include specific curriculum examples or standards, and AACTE considers it a starting point for deeper conversations among higher education institutions.

AI’s implications for training encompass many of the fundamentals of teaching candidates learn, including planning, assessment, differentiation, instructional choices, and professional ethics, said Anne Tapp Jaksa, a teacher education professor and senior research director of the University of Michigan’s Center for Digital Curricula who helped develop the framework. [...] The American Association of Colleges of Teacher Education released a new framework today calling for university-based teacher-education programs, which by federal estimates prepare more than 90% of new educators, to build a comprehensive approach to preparing teachers to understand how the technology can affect K-12 education—for good or ill.

AACTE, which represents more than 500 public and private college and university programs, also suggests that some aspiring teachers who oppose the technology on ethical grounds should be allowed to avoid using it and still receive their teaching credentials, a proposal that could be tricky for states to implement. [...] The framework says preservice teachers need explicit training on:

 Ethics and policy, such as AI literacy and equitable access.
 Practice and implementation, including being able to evaluate student work produced using AI tools.
 Cognitive issues both in the technology, such as biases and hallucinations, and in how the technology affects people, such as the effect of using AI on students’ critical thinking skills.
 Professional expertise, including how teachers use their own judgment and continue to build teacher-student relationships

items.title: Deep Cogito raises $43M Series A for AI self-improvement research - qz.com
items.summary: "Pre-training gives a model an enormous amount of knowledge and capability. Post-training determines
items.content:
"Pre-training gives a model an enormous amount of knowledge and capability. Post-training determines what that model can actually become," Arora said in a statement. "We believe the next frontier is in finding ways for models to improve their own intelligence, internalize those improvements, and become increasingly capable over time."

Deep Cogito's post-training engine powers two product lines: its Cogito family of open-weight models, which range from 3 billion to more than 600 billion parameters, and specialized models built on enterprises' proprietary data and outcomes. Unlike closed systems, open-weight models release their underlying numerical parameters for public use and typically carry lower operational costs. [...] Deep Cogito was founded in 2024 by Drishan Arora, who serves as chief executive, and Dhruv Malrana, chief product officer. The two co-founders had previously worked together at Google$GOOGL on AI Search — Arora led Gemini post-training for AI Search, while Malrana led its product from inception, the company said. [...] The startup's work centers on the post-training phase of AI development, the process that occurs after a model has been trained on large volumes of general data. Its research includes large-scale reinforcement learning and a technique called Iterated Distillation and Amplification, in which a model is given extra computation to generate answers it could not produce in one step, and those improved outputs are then folded back into the model's underlying parameters. Ultimately, the company aims to develop models capable of advancing their own intelligence independently, reaching a point where they are no longer constrained by the boundaries of human-generated training data.

本書定位與最終學習成果

定位：這不是只教聊天機器人 API 的應用書，而是一套由原理、資料、模型、訓練、評測、部署到治理的工程教材。全書以臺灣繁體中文、教育現場、半導體與製造、機器人及無人機等情境貫穿。

學生完成本書後，應能：

1. 由機率、token、attention 與 Transformer 元件解釋大模型的訓練與生成。

2. 從零實作 tokenizer、causal attention、Transformer block、MiniGPT 與訓練迴圈。

3. 建置具有來源、授權、個資處理、品質與版本紀錄的臺灣繁體中文語料。

4. 依算力選擇 continued pretraining、SFT、LoRA/QLoRA、偏好最佳化或 RAG。

5. 以臺灣任務、盲評、統計、安全與紅隊資料評估模型，而非只看全球排行榜。

6. 部署本地或雲端模型服務，量測延遲、吞吐、成本、記憶體、品質與可靠度。

7. 設計具引用、權限、工具、人類核准與稽核軌跡的 RAG/Agent/VLM 系統。

8. 提出能維護臺灣語言、文化、產業知識與資料主權的本土模型藍圖。

items.title: A football optimization–enhanced deep learning framework with large language model guidance for desalination systems - Nature
items.summary: The prediction of desalination system performance remains a critical challenge due to the complex, n
items.content:
The prediction of desalination system performance remains a critical challenge due to the complex, nonlinear, and multivariate nature of membrane-based processes, where data quality issues, feature redundancy, and suboptimal model configurations often undermine predictive reliability. Although deep learning models exhibit strong representational power, they are highly sensitive to preprocessing, feature selection, and hyperparameter tuning, while existing AutoML and rule-based optimization approaches are neither semantically aware nor sufficiently robust. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a joint data-oriented and optimization-based framework that integrates large language model (LLM)-controlled preprocessing with metaheuristic-driven feature selection and hyperparameter [...] metaheuristic-driven feature selection and hyperparameter optimization. Specifically, several state-of-the-art LLMs are evaluated for preprocessing and feature selection, while hyperparameter optimization of deep learning models, with a particular focus on Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Networks (STGCNs), is performed using the Football Optimization Algorithm (FbOA). Extensive experiments conducted on a synthetic desalination dataset demonstrate that FbOA consistently outperforms competing optimizers, yielding lower average prediction error, significantly reduced feature subsets, and improved stability. items.title: Nature Sub-Journal: Linguistic Diversity Rapidly Disappearing As 800 Million People Leverage AI For Writing - 36 Kr
items.summary: The research team first collected text corpora paired with authors' psychometric data, including age
items.content:
The research team first collected text corpora paired with authors' psychometric data, including age, gender, Big Five personality, empathy and moral values, then trained classifiers to predict these personal traits based on text features, and compared the prediction accuracy of original texts and LLM-rewritten texts. They found that:

First, the prediction accuracy drops by about 6% on average (absolute F1 value). The prediction performance of all six types of traits decreases significantly, among which age is the most affected: the F1 value falls from 0.351 to 0.260. However, the performance of the classifier is still above the random level. This indicates that AI has not completely erased the identity signals in the text, but only weakened these signals. [...] The first step is to observe real-world data. The research team analyzed three large-scale longitudinal datasets: arXiv paper abstracts (about 80,000), Patch News articles (about 379,600), and Reddit creative stories (about 318,000), with a time span from 2018 to 2024. They used the high-precision detection tool Binoculars to determine whether a text was AI-generated, and tracked the variance changes of the "writing complexity" indicator. The results are highly consistent: [...] arXiv: After the release of ChatGPT, the variance in writing complexity saw a significant and continuous decline, and changes in AI usage can significantly predict subsequent changes in variance. In other words, the more frequently AI is used, the more convergent the styles of academic writing become.
 Patch News: There was a sharp drop in variance when ChatGPT was launched, but the Granger causality test was not significant. The research team believes that professional editing processes and institutional norms may have buffered the homogenization effect of AI, yet subtle impacts still exist — it may not be direct usage, but AI-generated content plays an indirect role by influencing the overall writing norms.

Sarah Perez

Particle, the AI newsreader startup founded by former Twitter engineers, is shifting it
items.content:
Sarah Perez

Particle, the AI newsreader startup founded by former Twitter engineers, is shifting its focus to a potentially more lucrative idea: indexing the spoken conversations buried in podcasts and making them discoverable. On Wednesday, the company introduced Radar, a podcast search engine that not only transcribes podcast audio but also understands what it means, enabling it to pull out key quotes and highlights.

The solution has business potential, as it’s already attracted interest from hedge funds looking for data that their agents can’t see, explains Particle co-founder and CEO Sara Beykpour. [...] The alerts, which can be delivered via email, Slack, or webhook, can be customized with filters. These let users configure Radar to only send alerts when certain guests appear and discuss a particular topic, for instance. The search can also be narrowed in other ways such as limiting it to top podcasts only.

Radar can extract relevant self-contained clips, with timestamps, allowing users to both listen to and read the comments made.

“We’ve pre-chosen notable clips, so if you can’t listen to the whole podcast and you don’t want to read a summary, this is the best way to just get an idea of what’s happening in that podcast,” Beykpour noted. [...] 🚨 Flash Sale 🚨 Get $100 off your Disrupt 2026 ticket
